solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Reformed zodiac without date, without animals

indicators.note: the first 'without' tells us to leave a letter standing for date out of the word before it
something reformed has been made over into a new shape, so the remaining letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
D is the standard abbreviation for date

explanation.surface: Someone redraws the zodiac with no dates and none of its animal signs.
explanation.walkthrough: The zodiac is full of animals, which makes 'without animals' feel like more instructions; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Azoic describes geological ages or rocks with no trace of life, so it means lacking animal life.

clue.text: What's active in biting?

indicators.note: 'in' places the abbreviation for active inside the word that follows

blocks.note: acrid means sharp or biting, of a smell or taste
A is the grammatical abbreviation for active

explanation.surface: A riddle asking what creature is busy when something bites.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: A goes inside ACRID, and an acarid, a mite, is exactly the thing active when you are bitten.
explanation.definitionFit: An acarid is a mite or tick, a tiny arachnid whose bite is what is happening when one is active on the skin.

clue.text: Mine worker once locally gathering cobalt

indicators.note: a word gathering something collects it inside itself

blocks.note: onst is a dialect form of once
Co is the chemical symbol for cobalt

explanation.surface: A miner from a bygone era, speaking dialect, collects cobalt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Locally' marks a regional word, here the dialect form of once.
explanation.definitionFit: In mining an oncost worker was one paid by the day rather than by output, so an oncost is a kind of mine worker.

clue.text: Also old pair of lovers

blocks.note: first meaning: an archaic adverb meaning likewise, used to introduce each entry in a list
second meaning: a couple known to be romantically involved

explanation.walkthrough: 'Old' belongs to the first meaning, marking it as archaic, not to the lovers.
explanation.definitionFit: The word was once used in accounts for 'likewise', and today a couple who are dating are said to be one.

clue.text: Establish conservation company

blocks.note: con is a short form of conservation
a firm is a business company

explanation.surface: Someone sets up a conservation business.
explanation.definitionFit: To confirm something is to make it certain or settled, a synonym of establishing it.

clue.text: Endure endless revolutionary ego over outpouring of speech

indicators.note: endless means the final letter of the preceding word is cut off
a revolution turns things right round, so the shortened word is read from the other end

blocks.note: to suffer something is to endure it
the ego is the self, the I
on can mean over, as in a talk on or over a subject

explanation.surface: A revolutionary's ego goes on and on in a gushing speech.
explanation.walkthrough: SUFFER loses its last letter and is turned round to begin the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An effusion is an unrestrained flow of words or feeling, a gush of talk.

clue.text: Take more than a fair share after wharf cut round clam

indicators.note: cut means a letter is chopped off the end of the word for wharf
'after' sends the greedy word second, behind the shortened wharf

blocks.note: a quay is a wharf

blocks.clueFragment: Take more than a fair share
blocks.note: to hog is to take more than your share

explanation.surface: Someone greedy at a wharf takes too much of the catch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Round' seems to belong to the wordplay but it describes the clam.
explanation.definitionFit: The quahog is a thick-shelled, rounded edible clam of the North American Atlantic coast.

clue.text: Himalayan native funeral British avoided

indicators.note: the letter for British is avoided, so it is left out of the word for funeral

blocks.note: a burial is a funeral
B is the abbreviation for British

explanation.surface: A local man in the Himalayas had a funeral the British stayed away from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Native' suggests a person, but the native here is an animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The urial is a wild sheep found in the mountains of central Asia and the Himalayan region.

clue.text: Sweet child nurse running short on humour

indicators.note: running short means the word loses its final letter

blocks.note: an amah is a nurse or nanny in parts of Asia
bile was one of the four bodily humours of old medicine

explanation.surface: A lovely nanny is losing her sense of humour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Humour' is the old medical sense, one of the four bodily fluids.
explanation.definitionFit: Amabile is a musical direction meaning play sweetly or tenderly.

clue.text: What's not good for lorries ruined a long drive

indicators.note: something ruined is wrecked out of its proper shape, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A long haul has wrecked something, which is bad news for trucks.
explanation.definitionFit: Overlading is overloading a vehicle with cargo, which is bad for lorries, the British word for trucks.

clue.text: A piece of cake? I want it!

blocks.note: first meaning: something very easy, a sure thing
second meaning: a casual 'give me', a demand for something

explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a greedy child eyeing a slice of cake; 'piece of cake' is the idiom for an easy task.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for an easy success or concession, and also a slurred 'give me' used when demanding something.

clue.text: Plainsong format once composed

indicators.note: to compose is to put together in a new arrangement, so the letters are reordered

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Plainchant was a musical form that was once written down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Composed' fits the musical surface perfectly while doing the rearranging.
explanation.definitionFit: A canto fermo is the fixed melody of plainchant around which counterpoint was built, so it is plainsong.

clue.text: Made even compiler woolly

blocks.note: comp. is an abbreviation for compiler
lanate is a botanical term for woolly

explanation.surface: The setter has been woolly, but things were evened out.
explanation.definitionFit: Complanate means flattened or levelled, brought into one plane.

clue.text: Help over turning back sea — Canute's power, say

indicators.note: turned over means read the other way round
turning back means the next word is read from its end

blocks.note: aid is help
the Med is the Mediterranean Sea

explanation.surface: King Canute famously tried to make the sea turn back.
explanation.walkthrough: Canute was the English king said to have ordered the tide back; the clue evokes that legend.
explanation.definitionFit: A diadem is a crown, the emblem of royal power, as a king like Canute held.

clue.text: Very packed salon? Um … floor is failing

indicators.note: something failing is breaking down, so the letters collapse into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A crowded salon hesitates as its floor gives way under the weight.
explanation.definitionFit: A salon is a room, and a very packed one holds a roomful of people.

clue.text: Froth on beer? Pub server's no help

indicators.note: 'no' means the following word is taken away from the server

blocks.note: a barmaid serves in a pub
aid is help

explanation.surface: A frothy pint, and the barmaid is no help.
explanation.definitionFit: Barm is the yeasty froth that forms on fermenting malt liquor such as beer.

clue.text: Go away! I am one after quiet

indicators.note: 'after' puts the numeral for one behind the call for silence

blocks.note: I'm is short for I am
sh is a call for quiet
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone shouting 'clear off' declares they're number one after the hush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One after quiet' puts I after SH.
explanation.definitionFit: Imshi is army slang, from Arabic, telling someone to clear off.

clue.text: Seed pod, coloured, carried by wild lilies

indicators.note: wild means out of order, so the flowers' letters are scrambled
carried by means held inside the other letters

blocks.note: c. is an abbreviation for coloured
taken as written

explanation.surface: Coloured seed heads on wild lilies.
explanation.definitionFit: A silicle is a short broad pod of plants in the cabbage family, a kind of seed capsule.

clue.text: Language divide is very great around Gloucestershire

indicators.note: around means the outsize abbreviation is wrapped round the county abbreviation

blocks.note: taken as written
OS stands for outsize, very great
Glos is the abbreviation for Gloucestershire, an English county

explanation.surface: A big dialect boundary runs round an English county.
explanation.definitionFit: An isogloss is a line on a map dividing areas that differ in a linguistic feature.

clue.text: Drink with honey, orange rind and melon blended

indicators.note: a rind is the outer skin, so the outside letters are kept
blended means mixed together, so the fruit's letters are jumbled

blocks.note: the first and last letters of orange
taken as written

explanation.surface: A recipe for a honeyed drink with orange peel and blended melon.
explanation.definitionFit: Oenomel is an ancient Greek beverage of wine mixed with honey.

clue.text: Commander mounted reprisal, daring to lose some on the flanks

indicators.text: to lose some on the flanks
indicators.note: losing some letters on both flanks leaves a run from the middle of the phrase

blocks.note: the inner run of these two words once the outer letters go

explanation.surface: A cavalry officer launches a bold reprisal, with losses on both wings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flanks' fits the military scene but here means the ends of the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A risaldar was the commander of a troop of Indian cavalry, so a mounted commander.

clue.text: Puzzling emotion as one is flustered

indicators.note: someone flustered is thrown into disorder, so the letters are mixed up

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A baffling feeling comes over someone when flustered.
explanation.definitionFit: Anoesis is a state of pure sensation or emotion without understanding, which is a puzzling kind of feeling.

clue.text: Sad and low to note rare event

blocks.note: to feel blue is to feel sad
to low is to moo, like cattle
n. is an abbreviation for note

explanation.surface: Feeling sad and down, someone notes a rare occurrence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Low' is the cow's call, not the mood.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Once in a blue moon' means very rarely, so a blue moon is an occurrence that hardly ever happens.

clue.text: Gander finally swallowing eel

indicators.note: finally points to the very last letter of the next word

blocks.note: the last letter of swallowing
a lance is a sand eel

explanation.surface: A goose ends up gulping down an eel.
explanation.walkthrough: Gander looks like the male goose; it is slang for a quick look. 'Swallowing' is not a container here.
explanation.definitionFit: To take a gander is to have a quick look, a synonym of a glance.

clue.text: Seeming to question SNP's understanding about pound

indicators.note: about means the Scots word wraps around the letter for pound

blocks.note: uptak is the Scots form of uptake, understanding; the SNP is the Scottish National Party
L is the abbreviation for a pound sterling

explanation.surface: Scottish nationalists grasp something about the pound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'SNP's' marks the word as Scots, since the Scottish National Party is the Scottish independence party.
explanation.definitionFit: Uptalk is the rising intonation that makes statements sound like questions.

clue.text: Enclosure restraining missing canine

indicators.note: missing means the letter for canine is dropped from the word

blocks.note: chaining is restraining
C is the dental notation for a canine tooth

explanation.surface: A pen holding back a dog that has gone missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Canine' suggests a dog, but here it is the tooth, C in dental notation.
explanation.definitionFit: Haining is a dialect word for an enclosed or protected field or plot of land.

clue.text: I am surprised retiring milkmaid did dance

indicators.note: retiring means drawing back, so the word is read in reverse

blocks.note: ha is an exclamation of surprise
a dey is an old word for a dairymaid

explanation.surface: Someone is amazed that a shy milkmaid got up and danced.
explanation.definitionFit: The hay or hey is an old country dance, so to have hayed is to have danced it.

clue.text: Reactive substance, one mostly dug up

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter is used

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral one
mined means dug up from the earth

explanation.surface: A volatile chemical, much of it excavated.
explanation.definitionFit: An imine is an organic compound with a carbon-nitrogen double bond, often reactive in chemistry.

clue.text: Work protecting a little over forty hybrid species

indicators.note: protecting means surrounding and shielding the Roman numeral

blocks.note: op is short for opus, a work
XLI is the Roman numeral for forty-one

explanation.surface: A job that shelters a group of just over forty mixed-breed creatures.
explanation.definitionFit: The oxlip is a primula of hybrid origin between primrose and cowslip, often treated as its own species.

clue.text: In the year Hannibal's son abandons capital

indicators.note: abandoning the capital means dropping the initial, capital letter

blocks.note: Hanno is a Carthaginian name in Hannibal's family

explanation.surface: A historical note: in some year Hannibal's son left Carthage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' looks like a city such as Carthage, but it means the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Anno is Latin for 'in the year', as in anno Domini.

clue.text: Excellent drug support worker

blocks.note: E is slang for ecstasy
a leg supports a table
a worker ant

explanation.surface: Praise for a drug that supports workers.
explanation.definitionFit: Elegant can mean neat and first-rate, as an excellent solution is called elegant.

clue.text: Girl's accommodating over early game of hockey

indicators.note: accommodating means giving room inside, so a letter is housed within

blocks.note: a gal is a girl
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: A girl is in charge of an early hockey match.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'Girl's' is 'is'. The definition is an old sense, not the scoring target.
explanation.definitionFit: Goal was formerly the name of a ball game resembling hockey, an early form of the sport.

clue.text: Girl the reverse of game, for example

indicators.note: the reverse of means the following words are read backwards

blocks.note: nim is a game of taking objects from heaps
say means for example

explanation.surface: A girl doing the opposite of a game, for instance.
explanation.definitionFit: Yasmin is a girl's given name, a form of Jasmine.

clue.text: Like the first book a Cingalese composed

indicators.note: composed means put together in a new order, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Sri Lankan writer produced their first book.
explanation.walkthrough: Cingalese is an old spelling of Sinhalese, of Sri Lanka.
explanation.definitionFit: Genesiacal means relating to Genesis, the first book of the Bible.

clue.text: Defendant before law to bow down

blocks.note: def. is the abbreviation for defendant
lex is Latin for law

explanation.surface: A defendant before the law is made to bow down.
explanation.definitionFit: To deflex is to bend or turn downwards, so to bow down.

clue.text: Returning barges glide smoothly

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the word is read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: keels are flat-bottomed barges, used on the Tyne

explanation.surface: Barges coming back glide smoothly along.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleek as a verb can mean to move smoothly, to glide.
